text: Hibernation [Lat. hibernare , from hiems , winter]: Ger. Winterschlaf ; Fr. sommeil hibernal ; Ital. ibernazione . The state of torpor in which some animals which inhabit cold or temperate latitudes pass the winter. Long looked upon as a specially created provision, this peculiar state is now regarded as an adaptation fostered by natural selection. Literature : art. Hibernation, in Todd's Cyc. of Anat. and Physiol.; WESLEY MILLS, Hibernation and Allied States in Animals, Trans. Roy. Soc. of Canada (1892). ( C.LL.M. )
